items.stem: Point $B$ is symmetric to $A(1, 2)$ with respect to the line $x+2y-10=0$. Work out $B$ and tap it on the grid.
items.construction: Reflection of A(1,2) in x+2y-10=0: value at A is -5, normal (1,2), so B = (1,2) + 2(1,2) = (3,6). Midpoint (2,4) lies on the line (2+8-10=0) and AB is parallel to the normal. Tap (3,6), which is on the board (x -2..8, y -2..8).
items.predicate_meaning: Right distances, wrong signs — the point is in the wrong quadrant
items.hint: Check the signs when you solve the two equations.
items.why: Reflections of (3,6) in the axes, such as (-3,-6), (3,-6) and (-3,6), fall outside the board (x -2..8, y -2..8), so it can hardly fire here. The hint about 'signs when you solve the two equations' also doesn't fit this question, which has no such equations.

items.stem: Point $B$ is symmetric to $A(4, -1)$ with respect to the line $4x-2y-3=0$. Work out $B$ and tap it on the grid.
items.construction: Value of 4x-2y-3 at A = 16+2-3 = 15; |n|^2 = 20. B = A - 2*(15/20)*(4,-2) = (4,-1) - (6,-3) = (-2,2). Check: midpoint (1,0.5) gives 4-1-3=0, on the line; AB = (-6,3) is parallel to the normal (4,-2). (-2,2) lies in the default -5..5 grid, so tap it.
items.predicate_meaning: Plotted (y, x) — the pair read in the wrong order
items.hint: Check which of your two numbers is s (across) and which is t (up).

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of the circles $x^2+y^2=10$ and $x^2+y^2+2x-y=5$. Plot both points.
items.construction: Subtracting the circles gives y=2x+5. Substituting gives x²+4x+3=0, so x=-1 or -3, giving (-1,3) and (-3,-1). Both satisfy both circles: 1+9=10 and 1+9-2-3... =5; 9+1=10 and 10-6+1=5. Use the several-points form with targets [[-1,3],[-3,-1]] and the default grid -5..5. Tap both lattice points.
items.predicate_meaning: Right distances, wrong signs — the point is in the wrong quadrant
items.hint: Recheck the signs when finding y.
items.why: Fires when every wrong point is a target reflected, for example (1,3) and (3,-1), or (-1,-3) and (-3,1). Many of these come from a sign slip in x, such as solving x²+4x+3=0 as x=1,3, but the hint says to recheck signs when finding y. That misdirects the student, so it is not reliably helpful.
